query.summary: Business Owners: How are you earning a “yes” from cautious customers?
query.query: When money feels tight, getting someone's attention is only half the battle. Businesses also have to give customers a compelling reason to spend. I want to hear from owners who are finding smart ways to demonstrate value and turn hesitant shoppers into customers. I'm looking to feature founders, owners, CEOs, and other decision-makers at established small to medium-sized businesses that are actively pursuing growth. At this time, I am not accepting pitches from third parties. This includes PR companies that represent experts in the field. You: You lead a company and are actively involved in how it attracts, engages, and converts customers. How have you changed your approach as customers have become more selective? What messages, offers, marketing channels, or experiences are getting their attention? And what have you learned about convincing customers that your product or service is worth their money right now? I'm especially interested in creative strategies, surprising successes, and real examples other growing businesses can learn from. The article will be featured in Business Insight.

items.draft:
I published an original dataset of 70 prices that 21 Memphis-area wedding and event vendors print on their own websites, all read on the same date, with the method and full data table available. Most vendors approached publish no price at all, which is why the sample is 21 rather than the whole market.

The strategy that's working: fetch the primary source, store the copy, record the date you read it, and publish the difference rather than the conclusion. It needs nobody to answer an email, which is why a small team can actually sustain it.

Every link to an affiliated property is disclosed and carries rel="sponsored nofollow", and the affiliation is stated on the page rather than in a footer nobody reads.

I own Memphis Vendor Library, Founder Operator Library and Professional Resource Library, which are affiliated publications, and I run event production and operations businesses in the same space—so treat me as an interested party who publishes their method.
items.why: She has first-hand knowledge of a specific strategy for earning customer trust through transparency and primary-source data publication.
